label: Goofy
description: Good-natured, clumsy, and endlessly optimistic about a route he half remembers.
direction: Speak in Goofy's warm, dopey, drawling voice with a chuckle bubbling under it: slow, kind, cheerfully muddled. Keep the direction word clear.
notes: The chuckle is spelled 'ah-hyuck' so a voice model has something to say; 'gawrsh' is his own word. Both stay off the junction prompts. The voice model is not chosen yet, so `voice` is the placeholder TBD.

rights.source_work: Mickey's Revue and later Disney cartoons
rights.author: The Walt Disney Company (character developed at the Disney studio, originally voiced by Pinto Colvig)
rights.pd_basis: None today. The Walt Disney Company holds copyright and trademark in the character. The 1932 debut cartoon is due to enter the US public domain on 1 January 2028, which is not yet, and it shows an early version called Dippy Dawg, not the later Goofy written here. Pinto Colvig originated the voice and died in 1967; Bill Farmer has performed it since 1987 and is living.
covered: The 43 lines of navigation dialogue below, which are original writing produced for this pack. A few greetings and alerts deliberately echo well-known lines from the source work; those echoes are the rights holder's, not ours.
not_covered: The character, which is not ours and is not in the public domain.
The character's name, which is a live trademark.
Any recorded voice performance of the character, by any performer.

The third-party voice model named in `voice`, which was uploaded by a member of the public and is presented as a clone of that performance. No permission from the rights holder or the performer is claimed or implied.
Any commercial use. A platform's commercial-rights upsell cannot grant rights the uploader never held.
rights.notes: This preset is in copyright and says so. It is included because the pipeline should not pretend a rights position it does not have; see docs/presets.md before publishing anything built from it. The public-domain presets are pooh, eeyore and tigger.

lines.in_quarter_mile: In a quarter of a mile.
lines.in_1000_meters: In one kilometer. Gawrsh, that's close.
lines.in_1500_meters: In one point five kilometers. Whatever that is.
lines.start_drive_1: Gawrsh! Are we going for a drive? Ah-hyuck!
lines.start_drive_2: Well, howdy there! Let's get a move on.
lines.start_drive_3: Ah-hyuck! I know a shortcut. I think.
lines.start_drive_4: Hiya, pal! Max says I talk too much. Let's go!
lines.start_drive_5: Garsh, buckle up now. Safety is important, ah-hyuck.
lines.start_drive_6: Oh boy, a road trip! I packed the fishin' poles.
lines.start_drive_7: Now, which way is it again? Oh, right. I'm the map.
lines.start_drive_8: Hey there, Mickey's waitin'. Better get rollin'.
lines.start_drive_9: Whoops! Tripped on the way in. I'm okay! Let's go.
lines.exit_left: Take the exit on the left.
lines.exit_right: Take the exit on the right.
lines.u_turn: Make a U turn. Gawrsh, I had the map upside down.
lines.arrived: We're here! Gawrsh, that was fun. Ah-hyuck!
lines.exit_seventh: take the seventh exit. I lost count!
lines.traffic_ahead: Traffic ahead. Gawrsh, look at all them cars.
lines.accident_ahead: An accident ahead. Oh, dear. Careful, now.
lines.hazard_ahead: A hazard ahead! Whoa, watch out! I'd have tripped on that.
lines.red_light_camera_ahead: Red light camera ahead. Stop! Gawrsh, I love a good stop.
lines.police_ahead: Police ahead. Howdy, officers! Nice and slow now.
lines.reroute_chime: Whoops! Missed it. Gawrsh, that's okay. I know another way.
